executiveSummary: GM0531 passes the complete deterministic model contract for all ten canonical presets, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 CBS/PDOK identity, 32,859 residents, twelve neighbourhoods, one BAG place, one BRT woonkern, 28 scheduled-transit stop areas and six A15/A16/N915 municipal-border routes are coherent. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Hendrik-Ido-Ambacht is a low-lying Zwijndrechtse Waard municipality in IJsselmonde dike-ring trajectories 17-1 through 17-3, alongside the tidal Noord and with both protected and outside-dike exposure. The municipal vision says a primary-kering breach can flood almost the whole municipality and much of the built area up to 2.5 m in its cited stress test. Exact containment places two primary and two regional LIWO candidate points inside GM0531. The model selects none of them, yet reports an exact 2.721845 m generic river depth from T+12 through T+72, 20,561 affected people-equivalent and 1,196,129.91 person-hours by T+72; its separate coastal preset reports zero direct inundation despite official benedenrivieren evidence that sea level, tide, wind, storm-surge barriers and river discharge interact. Eight unrelated nonzero hazard families reuse one exact twelve-neighbourhood order. The graph omits the A15 Noordtunnel, movable N915 Bridge over the Noord, Waterbus fallback, Sophiaspoortunnel/Betuweroute, local road inundation, outside-dike access, industrial/toxic-release pathways, the sewer-to-RWZI Zwijndrecht chain, split Oasen/Evides drinking-water context, existing/planned heat-network dependencies and external acute care. Retain real flood eligibility, finite direct-wildfire support, non-residential demand and Mobility/Supply-only road scope. Suppress unsupported physical depth, local rank, affected, service and recovery precision. NoData, no selected case, a plan, a scheduled service, a completed past advisory or an observation never means zero, safe, operational or recovered.

evidenceSources.title: E01 — Wijken en buurten 2025, full administrative geometry, BAG place and BRT settlement

supports: Fresh CBS OData row GM0531 reports Hendrik-Ido-Ambacht, 32,859 residents, density 3,226/km², 5,784 residents age 65+ and 3,451 one-person households. CBS cells are independently rounded or suppressed and nulls are not zeros.

The current non-generalized GM0531 MultiPolygon has 785 coordinate positions, versus 43 positions in the generated overview geometry; the generated center [4.636400844672923, 51.837665632484196] lies inside both.

The consumed regional data contain twelve neighbourhoods, one active BAG place and one BRT woonkern. Administrative geography is observed/reference context, not a dike compartment, hydraulic domain, evacuation zone or utility topology.
CBS/administrative data are CC BY 4.0 and BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0. Edition, retrieval time, generalized/full-resolution role, coverage and missing-value semantics must remain visible.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Omgevingsvisie: climate, high-water safety and outside-dike business areas
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal environment vision published 2023; web pages and underlying 2021/2022 stress-test context retrieved 2026-09-03
supports: The municipality states that much ground lies one to two metres below NAP and that a primary-water-barrier breach can inundate almost the whole municipality; its cited stress test shows much of the built area with depths up to 2.5 m.

At a frequent 1-in-10-year outside-dike scenario, published context confines exposure mainly to Sophiapolder, Crezéepolder and the area between Ringdijk and Noordpark; a 1-in-100 case also reaches parts of the center. Different probability/scenario classes must not be merged.

The vision identifies extreme-rain road impassability, overloaded sewers, high/future groundwater, heat on paved residential/business areas, land subsidence, water-quality effects and salinity sensitivity of the Noord during low flow.
Veersedijk's water-related industry/worker homes developed outside the dike; Antoniapolder is water-bound beside the Noord and A15/A16 and permits high environmental categories up to 5.2.

These maps and policy pages have no live event cadence, complete native raster/NoData contract or standard open-data reuse licence stated. They support eligibility and planning, not current depth, probability, passability or operational state.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Hendrik-Ido-Ambacht and Waterschap Hollandse Delta
evidenceSources.title: E03 — Water- en Rioleringsprogramma 2025–2029 and RWZI service-area register
evidenceSources.edition: Final version dated 2024-12-02 for 2025–2029; current official WSHD service-area page retrieved 2026-09-03
supports: The final programme reports 175 km free-flow sewer, 25 km pressure/force mains, 33 sewer pumping stations, 145 pressure-sewer pump units, five stormwater-settling basins, 13,300 gullies and 4,100 inspection pits.

Major basins/pumps use telemetry and alarms; two main sewer pumps and the main force main toward RWZI Zwijndrecht are water-board managed. WSHD independently lists Hendrik-Ido-Ambacht in RWZI Zwijndrecht's service area.

The 2024 BRP calculates water on street mainly at the stormwater system for design storm 08 (19.8 mm/hour). The programme reports subsidence/lost storage, groundwater ingress and sinkhole priority, generally high groundwater, regular complaints and 33 telemetered monitoring wells.

The municipality's 2019 sewer incident plan is linked to the Zwijndrechtse Waard water-overload plan and outside-dike high-water plan. Plan existence is not proof of live activation, readiness, staffing or completed actions.

Asset condition, nominal monitoring and annual maintenance are policy/engineering evidence, not current failure, compatible pump capacity, receiving-water state or guaranteed recovery. The PDF states no standard reuse licence or live machine cadence.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028 and Veiligheidsrapportage 2024
evidenceSources.edition: Regional profile adopted 2024-12-05 for 2025–2028; municipal safety report covers 2024
supports: The profile places Hendrik-Ido-Ambacht in IJsselmonde dike ring 17 and covers trajectories 17-1 through 17-3, outside-dike flooding, regional-barrier breach and extreme rainfall. Not all regional primary trajectories met the completed first assessment's standards.

Hendrik-Ido-Ambacht has an adopted outside-dike high-water response plan. The municipal report says high water, flood threat and evacuation are increasingly prominent and describes exercises in 2024; exercises and plans are not current incidents or completed checkpoint actions.

Regional transport of dangerous goods uses A15, A16, water, rail and pipelines; the Noord/Merwede/Oude Maas junction is intensely navigated, and the tunnel under the Noord and Sophiaspoortunnel are identified transport-incident contexts.

The municipal safety report identifies Bolidt as risk-relevant because of hazardous-material storage. Its 2024 exercise evacuated De Blije Borgh and YES! childcare after a simulated energy-house explosion; the scenario is preparedness evidence, not an actual event or current facility state.

Strategic/planning PDFs have no live machine cadence or standard data-reuse licence stated and do not establish current likelihood, perimeter, resources, route state, vulnerable occupancy or response completion.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — LIWO 2025.1.6 candidate catalogues and benedenrivieren hydraulic semantics
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO application 2025.1.6; dataset project 2025_0_1; official benedenrivieren guidance current at retrieval
supports: Exact containment against the generated municipality geometry places primary candidates 1950, Noord km 978, and 1951, Noord km 980.5, inside GM0531. It also places regional Waal candidates 1236 at Achterambachtseweg and 1237 at Dorpstraat inside; bbox-only records from neighbouring municipalities were rejected.

No regional-water-system candidate is returned inside the query envelope. The one outside-dike catalogue point is outside GM0531; this no-match does not erase the municipality's evidenced outside-dike areas or high-water plan.
A candidate point/frequency flag does not select a breach, defence/overtopping state, hydrograph, probability, connected footprint or consequence grid.

Official benedenrivieren guidance states that river discharge, sea level/tide, wind and storm-surge barriers jointly determine high water. Separate straight-line coast and major-river proximity fields cannot represent that coupling.

Causal use requires specialist selection and pinned release, scenario/model dates, source water, breach/overtopping/control variant, native CRS/resolution/units/NoData, depth, velocity, arrival, duration, recession and scenario-clock mapping. Exact redistribution terms for persisted LIWO products require confirmation.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — NWB routes, Noord crossings, Betuweroute and scheduled transit
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-light 2026-08-01; ProRail OGC current at retrieval; OVapi schedule valid 2026-08-30 through 2026-12-12; RWS project pages current 2026-09-03
supports: The A15 Noordtunnel beneath the Noord connects Hendrik-Ido-Ambacht and Alblasserdam, has no emergency shoulders and is monitored/operated 24/7; renovation is planned for 2027–2028. Planned works are not a current closure or reduced capacity.

The movable N915 Bridge over the Noord is a distinct crossing. Its 2023–2026 renovation is published as complete; past closures used the Noordtunnel for general vehicles, but ADR traffic could not use that tunnel and needed long alternative routes. Waterbus served cyclists/pedestrians.

ProRail's network context places the Betuweroute/Sophiaspoortunnel near/through Hendrik-Ido-Ambacht and Kijfhoek. The generated municipality has no passenger-rail station; the municipality describes Zwijndrecht and Dordrecht as external stations.

The deployed schedule has 28 stop areas including Waterbus Noordeinde. Static rail/road geometry and scheduled stops do not prove incident operation, vehicles, passenger/freight presence, accessible evacuation capacity or emergency exemptions.
NWB road geometry and ProRail OGC are CC0; OVapi is free/best-effort schedule context. Structure, mode, source/valid time, restriction, detour and NoData must remain explicit.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Business parks, hazardous-material routing and environmental supervision

supports: OZHZ's high-supervision list includes Bolidt chemical industry with risk score 8 and hazardous-material storage, plus waste-processing, tank/metal work and multiple licensed shipbuilding/shipyard businesses. The municipality lists five business areas; Antoniapolder is water-bound beside the Noord/A15/A16, Veersedijk/Rietbaan hosts mainly shipyards and shipbreaking, and Ambachtsezoom/De Sandeling lie by A16.

A municipal dangerous-goods route was adopted 2020. The regional profile identifies transport on A15/A16, water, rail and pipelines. A legal route does not provide live cargo, commodity, quantity, vehicle position or release state.

The municipality notes relatively nearby Chemours/DuPont influence and regional PFAS concerns, while current environment/air pages direct users to responsible authorities. Context does not establish a GM0531 acute release or exposure.

These are regulatory/planning evidence without a continuous incident feed, dispersion field or standard reuse licence stated. Current source, release rate, meteorology, indoor/outdoor population, protective action and measurement remain Unknown.

findings.summary: Hendrik-Ido-Ambacht's 2025 identity, full boundary, neighbourhoods, settlement and demographic controls are coherent.

findings.summary: Real dike-ring flood eligibility is converted into unsupported exact local consequences without selecting a breach or hydraulic case.
findings.evidence: E02/E04/E05 establish dike ring 17, extensive potential inundation, outside-dike exposure and two contained primary/two regional candidates. The model selects none while fixing 2.721845 m T+12–72, 20,561 affected T+24–72 and 1,196,129.91 person-hours by T+72 without source water, forecast, defence/breach/overtopping/control, footprint, arrival, duration, recession or NoData.

Suppress metre claims, neighbourhood ranks, affected counts and dependent service/recovery precision until a water-manager-selected LIWO case supplies the complete causal contract. Keep primary, regional and outside-dike pathways separate and missing cells Unknown.

findings.summary: The zero direct coastal result is a false all-clear for a hydraulically coupled benedenrivieren municipality.
findings.evidence: E02/E04 place GM0531 beside the Noord in IJsselmonde dike ring and document outside-dike high-water planning. E05 states benedenrivieren levels depend jointly on river discharge, sea level/tide, wind and storm-surge barriers. The coastal preset reports zero direct inundation at every checkpoint solely from open-coast distance while still generating wind/service burden.
findings.action: Retain zero only for the narrow direct open-coast distance contribution. Suppress any all-water/coastal-safety interpretation and implement selected tidal/storm-surge/river/barrier scenarios with explicit source and control states; do not simply enable an arbitrary coastal depth.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated hazards reuse one exact twelve-neighbourhood ranking.

Neither contained breach candidates/outside-dike areas, sewer routing, paved heat surfaces, cyber boundaries, industrial sources nor wind-aware smoke determines this order.
findings.action: Replace the shared seed with hazard-family-specific eligible domains and event-valid surfaces. Add a GM0531 unsupported note now and regression-test that unrelated hazards cannot silently publish an identical full local order.

Until then suppress local depth/rank/affected precision and never rasterize report figures.

residualLimitations: This audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a forecast, warning, flood assessment, evacuation plan, industrial-plume model, public-health instruction or operator commitment.
CBS values are rounded/suppressed and neighbourhood totals need not equal the municipality total; null district-heating/charging and absent operational records remain Unknown.
The overview boundary is selection/aggregation geometry only; full-resolution and native dike, outside-dike, hydraulic, sewer, road, rail, industrial and asset geometry is required for intersection.
LIWO candidate points and scenario maps require expert selection and complete release/model/spatial/NoData provenance; point presence is not breach, probability or connected inundation.
The municipal up-to-2.5 m and probability-class maps are planning/stress-test context, not validation of the generic 2.721845 m model value or a current event.
Benedenrivieren water levels couple river discharge, sea level/tide, wind and barrier operation; open-coast and river proximity screens cannot be interpreted independently as physical hydraulics.
WRP/HWH/WSHD assets do not establish connected catchments, compatible throughput, live controls, power/backup, receiving levels, overflow, quality or restoration.
OZHZ/municipal industrial records identify eligibility/supervision, not current inventory, release, plume, exposed population, firefighting resources, compliance or environmental effect.
NWB/NDW/ProRail/GTFS and operator project pages do not establish incident-time road/tunnel/bridge/rail/Waterbus state, vehicles, emergency exemptions, evacuation capacity or care reachability.
Oasen's June 2026 advisory was a completed past state; neither its lifting nor one Waterinfo/air/weather observation proves future or municipality-wide safety.

No complete public physical electricity, gas, heat, drinking-water, wastewater, telecom, facility, fuel, stock, staff, backup, repair or restoration topology is consumed; sensitive gaps remain Unknown or synthetic.
Resident allocation omits workers, care/childcare occupants, school users, visitors, evacuees, responders and road/rail/waterway transients at event time.
Direct wildfire zero is supported only as a narrow no-eligible-IPO-nature/no-selected-ignition result; urban/industrial fire and regional smoke are separate pathways.
Earthquake, cyber, heat, winter and severe-storm presets remain generic exercises unless a named event/target and valid-time forcing are selected.
The 72-hour horizon excludes prolonged displacement, contamination, health effects, economic/process losses, environmental remediation, reconstruction and adaptive behaviour.
